newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil confirms Norne start up delay.
newsitem.headline: Statoil confirms Norne start up delay.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Friday the start up of Norne oil development in the Norwegian Sea would be delayed by a month to sometime in August.
The state Norwegian oil company was confirming a report in the daily Stavanger Aftenblad newspaper.
Norne is being developed via a production ship and a system of subsea wells. It was originally planned to come on stream in July.
Statoil spokeswoman Nina Steihaug said the delay was due to extra work needed on the vessel.
"The ship was not delivered in the condition as was expected so there is more work to be done than we had foreseen," Steihaug said. The additional work would cost about 150 million crowns.

"Norne is still a profitable and good project. It (the rise in costs) is unfortunate but the project still comes within budget. We originally budgeted around 11 billion crowns and that has been reducing all the time down to 7.3 billion, now we're back to 7.5 billion," Steihaug said.
